overview.oneLineTake: Fear is still priced into tech, so stay defensive on short premium until CPI and Nvidia headlines settle.
themes: AI trade is under pressure: Thursday's tech rout pushed Nasdaq into correction territory, with Nvidia in a bear market and the Magnificent 7 losing about $1 trillion in a day.
Friday's bounce looks fragile: QQQ closed at 656.10, up 1.4%, and Dow futures lean lower into the open after Nvidia's board opened a probe into CEO Jensen Huang's alleged ties to a Chinese spy.
Rates are a headwind: October payrolls added 165,000 jobs with unemployment at 4.1%, the 10-year sits near 4.84%, and the Bank of England has hiked while the Fed is expected to lean hawkish.
Post-midterm politics: a Democratic sweep brings tariff, AI buildout and data center scrutiny, which hits high-multiple tech hardest.
CPI and PPI this week are the next test for the rate path and for profit margins.
risks: Nvidia headline risk and further AI de-risking at the open.
Iran: Trump calls renewed strikes unlikely if talks progress but keeps the option open.
Hot inflation prints would reinforce the rate hike narrative and pressure long-duration equities.
Retail selling is elevated and VIX surged on Thursday, so gap risk stays high.

intelligence.headline: Wall Street's Script Gets Flipped by Post-Election Rout
intelligence.summary: US stock futures pointed higher after the Nasdaq 100 sank 6.4% on Thursday, wiping out $2.3 trillion in the biggest drop since 2020, as traders who expected a post-election rally were wrong-footed.

intelligence.headline: Stock Market Today: Futures Rebound After Nasdaq Rout

intelligence.headline: Asia Hedge Funds, Rich Investors Face Steep Losses in AI Selloff
intelligence.summary: The selling sent a benchmark for Asian stocks down almost 4%, while UK and European stocks suffered smaller losses and oil prices dipped.

intelligence.headline: Crowded Hedge Fund Trades Are Unwinding Fast After Ugly October
intelligence.summary: Hedge fund losses are adding to unease as strategies meant to behave independently lose money in lockstep, exposing crowded positions and heavy leverage after a rough October.
